subject: Suggested example to illustrate HMC vs Gibbs

messages.author: 83aa4ea66d984b54
messages.subject: Suggested example to illustrate HMC vs Gibbs
parts: Sorry if this has been discussed before, I couldn't see anything in the forum. To present advantages of StataStan to Stata users, who have some built-in Gibbs/M-H functionality, is there an example people would particularly suggest? I want to keep it a realistic prospect for most users, with reasonable numbers of observations and parameters, but maybe some unpleasantly correlated parameters? Something like the example in the NUTS paper.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Suggested example to illustrate HMC vs Gibbs
parts:
Our go to is usually a hierarchical model — the 8 schools
model is great because it’s relatively small but still really
hard to fit with Random Walk Metropolis and Gibbs.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Suggested example to illustrate HMC vs Gibbs
parts:
On Monday, August 10, 2015 at 7:03:55 AM UTC-4, Robert Grant wrote:
Sorry if this has been discussed before, I couldn't see anything in the forum. To present advantages of StataStan to Stata users, who have some built-in Gibbs/M-H functionality, is there an example people would particularly suggest? I want to keep it a realistic prospect for most users, with reasonable numbers of observations and parameters, but maybe some unpleasantly correlated parameters? Something like the example in the NUTS paper.

The eight schools example is good for illustrating sampling pathologies, but it is sort of weird substantively and depending on how you do it, you may find that the group-level variance is near zero.

I just do a flat probit model. Gibbs with data-augmentation will perform well and Stan will perform almost equally well. One-parameter-at-a-time Gibbs or M-H will perform worse than Stan. Then, you can do an ordinal probit model where Gibbs with data-augmentation will perform worse than Stan because of the cutpoints update.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Suggested example to illustrate HMC vs Gibbs
parts:
One thing to keep in mind is that there are two motivations:

1) Stan is faster than everyone else.
2) Stan gets the right answer when everyone else doesn't.

Different models are compatible with the two motivations.
My own interests lie in the latter, hence hierarchical model
examples.

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Suggested example to illustrate HMC vs Gibbs
parts:
Hi, Robert regarding StataStan in particular, Bob Carpenter and Daniel Furr did some simulations comparing StataStan to Stata’s built-in Bayes, and StataStan wins by orders of magnitude.  The examples are item response models and hierarchical models, they’re the sort of applications that people want to use Bayes for.

I’m ccing Bob and Daniel and Sophia who should be able to send you the details.

Andrew
